subject: Re: PAIDF Next Steps — Partner Qualification & GTC Berlin Target
text:
Great, makes sense. Let’s add Protex too, since they’re topical here.

@Eric Landau<mailto:eric@encord.com> do you have 10 minutes today for a very quick call?

Context: we’re lining up a report for SDG partners for Jensen ahead of the June 2 release, now that we have more clarity on use-case-specific PAIDF software drops.

We’d like to include Encord in the report, but we need a few clearly defined use cases plus the error rate before SDG. Customer can be tbc - but we can try and align it to one as we progress.

Given the short runway, do you have any internal model use cases or benchmark examples we can use for “error rate before SDG”? Even directional numbers or representative internal examples would help.

The types of use cases we’re thinking about include

Area
Example Use Cases
Detection / Attribute Classes
Augmentation Variables
ITS
Weather detection, wrong-way vehicle, license plate recognition
vehicles, plates, road users, weather states
weather, time of day, traffic density, road condition
AOI
Glass inspection
defect / non-defect, crack, scratch, contamination
lighting, glare, material condition, background
Public Safety - PAS
People attribute search
hair type, hat type, backpack, clothing
camera angle, lighting, occlusion, crowd density
Public Safety - Action Recognition
Smoking/vaping, running, climbing
person action classes
pose, viewpoint, lighting, background
Industrial / Protex-style Safety
PPE compliance, near-miss detection, unsafe zone entry, forklift/person interaction
person, forklift/truck, PPE, zones, actions
lighting, camera angle, floor condition, occlusion, traffic density

We can align the final examples to whichever ones have the clearest baseline error rates before SDG. This could align nicely with Cosmos Embed work for CVPR.

Thanks,

Angus

subject: Re: Request for Meeting on Security Requirements and Deployment Options
text:
Hi Leo,
I understand the confusion. We are still on the same page, so there’s no need to worry.

To clarify what I meant by “support”:

  *
I don’t need direction implementation support after initial set up, as I will assign a software engineer on our side.
  *
However, if there are Encord-specific questions, we would need your team’s input. Or if there is critical bug from your side, this should be managed which should be “outside" of support hours.
  *
Again, we don’t expect significant hands-on work from Encord—this is mainly a Q&A-type support, since we are strong in ML/AI but not experts in Encord.

Given that, my concern comes from “20 hours” that is not very clear to me. Above Q&As to successfully deploy Encord are outside of this support, correct? If so, I think this 20 hours makes sense.

For your information, Voxel team also did not support any direct integration - just helped us for Q&A to solve our problems regarding to how to use Voxel SDK.

Thanks,
Hyungyu
